utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case number IT-00-39-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Krajisnik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. The appearances, as I see, Mr. Harmon is not there for the Prosecution, but Mr. Tieger and Mr. Hannis are there, and the whole Defence team is present. Before we continue with the cross-examination of Witness 018, I'd just like to verify a change in the order of calling witnesses, which is that today we will continue the cross-examination of Witness 018, then we certainly will have some time left. The Chamber has not seen yet, but I was informed that the Defence has filed submissions in respect of the time of the testimony of Mr. Deronjic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, it's a little bit wider than that. It's certainly -- it's a Defence motion which includes two points, one, that Mr. Deronjic has been notified after that deadline, which was set some considerable time ago, but there's also another substantive point, which is that we're saying that Mr. Deronjic should not give evidence in circumstances in which he find himself at the moment, which is that he is awaiting sentence in his own case. That is it in a nutshell, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I mainly refer to that second point. Of course, we'll have a look at the first point as well. Since Mr. Deronjic has been scheduled for Thursday, the Chamber would like to take a decision on the submissions. Is the Prosecution ready to either, in writing or orally, give its position in respect of these two questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, we had not seen the written filing yet. We knew it was coming and we had indicated to your staff yesterday that we would try to be prepared to make an oral argument as soon as possible after seeing the written submission. That might be possible later today if we have a chance to read it. We certainly would be able to do it tomorrow. We think we might have some time tomorrow as well after we finish those 92 bis witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber would like to be informed whether the Prosecution would be ready today and if so this courtroom is available and we would not risk that we're running out of time. So therefore, if it could be done today -- I mean, the Chamber also has to think it all over and to take a decision, and if the oral argument would be only tomorrow, then of course we would have less time for considering the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Would it be possible, Your Honour, to have a short break after we finish with this witness this morning before we do the argument, perhaps an hour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think that would be possible. We'll try to arrange for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That gives the Chamber also time to read the written submission. Then I do understand that tomorrow we have two 92 bis witnesses, Suad Dzafic and Nijaz Dubicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. The Chamber regrets that, for logistic reasons, we're not using our time in full, and hopes and expects that this is an incident and not the beginning of a tradition. Then Madam Usher, would you please escort the witness into the courtroom. Let's just have a look, because we have to go into private session first, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that the technicians have been instructed not to show the face of the witness when entering the courtroom on the screen, and I also do understand that the public gallery is empty at this moment, so that the face distortion is effective. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. There's one matter too. This witness, when he came, brought a new document with him that I had intended to tender when I read his summary before the cross-exam began. I spoke with Mr. Stewart this morning, and if it's agreeable with you, Mr. President and Your Honours, I would like to show him that exhibit and tender it at this time, before we continue with the cross-examination. It's his release from Batkovic camp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It was already indicated on the list. Any --

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: No objection at all, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objection. Then perhaps it would be the best that we start with that, and then we'd continue the cross-examination. Madam Usher, please escort the witness into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness 018, may I remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony. Please be seated. Before the Defence will continue to cross-examine you, first, the Prosecution will put one or more additional questions to you. That will not take much time. Mr. Hannis, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. May the witness be shown the next item, and may that be given the next number in our order.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P31.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. I do understand that we have a redacted version, and I see that the redacted version is now presented to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Examined by Mr. Hannis:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness 018, would you take a look at that document and tell us if you know what it is.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is my decision on the release from the Batkovic camp.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And is that a true copy of the original that you brought with you before you came to Court this week?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the copy before you has certain portions redacted or blacked out; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And are those portions ones that have your name or a number that would help identify you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I have no other questions, Your Honour. I would like to tender that into evidence at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. Hannis. Mr. Stewart, you may proceed your cross-examination. Cross-examined by Mr. Stewart:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good morning. Before the break on Friday, I asked you, through the Tribunal, His Honour asked you if you would over that break attempt to prepare a list of the 22 different types of uniform which in your evidence you say you saw in Brcko in early May 1992. Have you been able to do that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have such a list with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't actually see it. I suppose it's coming out of your pocket now.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: First of all, were you able to draw up a full list of 22 different types of uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and I added one more. So there's a total of 23.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. In the first place, I'd ask you to please run very quickly through that list. I don't mean so quickly that we can't hear and the interpreters can't deal with it, but what I mean is not stopping to describe any individual item in any detail. Just so that we get the overall picture, I wonder if you could just go very briefly in what I might call bullet-point form through the 23 items.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Last time, I mentioned a few of those uniforms. I told you what they looked like, and I can explain that again. There are about seven uniforms which are directly part of the JNA uniform by colour. There are two or three uniforms which were worn by the civilian protection and the Territorial Defence. Then there were a couple of camouflage uniforms, fully camouflaged uniforms, including the clothes and the footwear. Then there are different combinations: Military shirts or military pants. Then there were also those who wore black leather uniforms. These were part of special units. They perhaps worked as snipers. Then there were some uniforms which were completely black, with the Subara hats and the skull-and-crossbones insignia on the hat. And then there were also some people who even wore their sports equipment. So these are just a few examples. A characteristic of all of the above-mentioned was that they all wore high military boots, which at the time in the former Yugoslavia was a special thing because this was something that you were not able to buy freely. All the uniforms that I mentioned, or all the people wearing these uniforms, had white ribbons tied around their arms. This was for a couple of days. Then a couple of days later, they changed the colour of this band, so the colour was now purple and white. It was multicoloured. So this is what the situation was for those few days, up to about the 5th or the 6th of May.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you got all -- those are categories you've given us, then, but you have the different uniforms listed as numbers 1 to 23, do you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's take them one by one then. Start at number 1.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Military uniform of the SMB colour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that's -- SMB is -- it will -- I don't know how it will come back to you in translation, Witness, but SMB is what in English we'd call grey-olive.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did that signify to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were uniforms of the JNA and that uniform, members wearing that uniform, took part in the attack on Brcko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was that uniform that you've just mentioned, was that a camouflage uniform or just a plain olive-grey uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, no. It was of a single colour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And item 2?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Uniform of military officers of SMB, olive-grey colour, with a yellow band. This uniform was worn by military officers of a certain category.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that's -- the yellow band signifies a rank; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This was worn by military officers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Do I understand that it's -- in effect, it's the same as item 1 but with an indication of a higher rank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And item 3?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same uniform but now with a red band.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Signifying what?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A different kind of rank.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Item 4?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: SMB military uniform, but a winter uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And how does that differ in appearance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The difference is in the quality of the material. The material is thicker. It's of a different material than the summer uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, that's an unsurprising answer, Witness, and I can accept that, of course. But does it -- apart from the thickness of the material, what does it look like? Colour? What colour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They're all the same colour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the only difference there, not surprisingly, from summer to winter, is the type of thickness of the material; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Item 5?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same uniform but a summer uniform. The material is thinner, but it's of the same colour. The difference is in the fact that the summer uniform has a jacket and the winter uniform has a long coat.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So your item -- items 4 and 5 are the winter and summer SMB uniforms?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So is your item 1, then, the SMB military uniform, is that something different altogether from either items -- from items 4 and 5?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The difference between them is in the year of manufacture. All the ones so far, for example, the winter one, they're all replaced every few years. So the quality and the appearance is different, so that you can very easily notice the age of the uniform, how soiled it is, and you can tell the difference between such uniforms and new uniforms. It's very easy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not quite sure that that's dealing with the point. The question is this: You refer to winter uniform as item 4 and summer uniform as item 5, but are you saying that there is --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Are you saying there was some other JNA SMB uniform which was neither summer nor winter, but something else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those who wore the military uniforms as described in item 1 were mostly those who had been demobilised, and they were military personnel who were in service at the time. The people who had the winter and the summer uniforms were the ones who had been mobilised or who had come from somewhere. I don't know, because I didn't know any of those people that I saw. So those people who were issued uniforms earlier, they were probably people who had been mobilised in order to participate in the war in Bosnia, and they participated in the attack on Brcko.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. You've told us that. The -- I'm concerned to be clear at this point about the physical appearance and description of the uniforms. Just for clarity's sake, then, just indicate as a matter of physical description of the uniform how item 1 differs from both items 4 and 5 on your list.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to clarify. Under item 1, the military uniform of the SMB, olive-grey colour, in its appearance, these were newer-looking uniforms, while the SMB winter uniform and the SMB summer uniform differed from that in their quality and the service, the length of service. So you could obviously see that the number 1 item uniforms were newer than the uniforms as described in items 4 and 5. You could see the wear and tear in these other uniforms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Apart from newness, then, was item 1, in your view, correctly described as either summer or winter?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not really. It was May, and it was already the time to wear the summer uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That doesn't quite answer the question. Yes, it was May. Yes, that is early summer. But was the item, the military uniform that you have listed as number 1, was that a summer or a winter uniform, or neither?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was both. It was combined. Some people wore summer uniform tops and pants were part of the winter uniform, or it was the other way around. But they did wear all military uniforms. Those under items 4 or 5, however, wore either the full summer uniform or the full winter uniform.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What's item 6 on your list, then, Witness?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a camouflage uniform of yellow and green colour. It's multicoloured.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Multicoloured or two colours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were two colours combined, and the patterns were leaf-shaped or something like that. These were camouflage uniforms used in camouflage.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As they would be. And what did that uniform signify to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw that uniform before the bridges were destroyed. I saw it at the garrison, the barracks of the JNA in Brcko as I was passing along the fence. I saw those people who used to sit near the fence, in the evening, in these uniforms, and they would provoke any passers-by who were passing by the fence. They would just say things to them. And they were sitting there and wearing these camouflage uniforms, the yellow-green ones. Before that, I said that the barracks were relocated to another location, which was about 20 kilometres away from Brcko. So there were no conscripts there any more. And this fact indicated to me that now there were either paramilitary formations who had arrived there or some special forces.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you saying that particular uniform, item 6, didn't in itself signify membership of any particular group, but that the link, as far as you're concerned, is with what you observed in the barracks before the bridge was blown?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What's item --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mentioned -- may I continue?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I noticed these people, and I mentioned at the last hearing that those people came with that military officer who was in charge of resolving the situation and making sure that there was no unrest in the town. They came with him, and they were billeted at the barracks. The barracks still exists today in town, but it is now being used as a court.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What's item --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a courthouse.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. What's item 7 on your list, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 7 is a full camouflage uniform, except the colours are brown and light green.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did that signify to you at the time?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction. Brown and light yellow.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They were probably worn by some other units for some other purposes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Item 8?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Uniform of active police of light blue colour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Item 9?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Uniform of the reserve police, of dark blue colour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Item 10?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Uniform of the police which was worn 10 to 12 years before the war, and the difference was in the colour. It was not the same shade of blue that the police wore at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Item 11?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Blue uniform worn by the civilian protection. And I can tell you right away that those people who wore that uniform didn't have weapons, but they were in charge of securing different facilities, for example, shops or some companies, some supermarkets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. When you say "civilian protection," what -- you're talking about some specific, organised, official group, are you, or organisation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The civilian protection was formed at the level of the town, and in case of some kind of disaster, atomic strike or an earthquake, they were there to assist the population. They were there to help in case of a disaster. They didn't have weapons, but they did have different kinds of equipment, for example a Red Cross or a first-aid kit, and at the same time they were guarding or securing different facilities. They were just physically present there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And they were all local people, were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. So the employees of those companies were the ones guarding their own buildings, and there were also people in local communes across various neighbourhoods of town who were in charge of that task.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What you described as a blue uniform, that was in fact something that looked pretty much like workers' overalls; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not really. It was a blue uniform, just as the military uniform, only the colour was blue, a distinct blue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Uniform in the sense of separate trousers and jacket?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What's your item 12, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same kind of uniform, but they were worn by the Territorial Defence, and the Territorial Defence also carried weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Item 13?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dark-blue fatigues, overalls. That means a one-piece suit.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. So that's -- that was what I was suggesting to you a moment ago in relation to item 11. So what did that uniform signify for you at the time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you right now very specifically that that uniform was worn by the volunteers of Captain Dragan, who guarded us outside the SUP building, and on that terrace in the old Posavina Hotel and on the terrace later.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So then item 14?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later come various combinations. A uniform with different kinds of trousers. Working bottoms combined with different tops. But the trousers were blue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That sounds a bit different from some of the other items. Then what are you saying was the -- are you saying there was a common, clear identifying feature of what you have listed as item 14?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The items I described so far were, in my mind, and still are, very directly linked to the command of the army. The items that come later are linked in my mind with volunteer units, which numbered four or five, and they had distinguishing elements. They would have blue, either denim or normal trousers, or tracksuit bottoms, combined with different tops. The top could be a military shirt or something else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Among these are two uniforms -- if you let me finish.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Among these are two uniforms, including black leather suits, always worn by snipers, in my experience.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to stop you there just for this reason: To make sure that we're proceeding clearly. Because your most recent answer suggests that you're going into the later items on your list. That's correct, isn't it? The summary that you've just given relates to -- not just to item 14 but to some of the other items from 15 to 23; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. To cut a long story short, I only wanted to explain the two --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, the cutting of the story short will largely be done by me, please, if you answer the questions. Let's stick with item 14 or the moment and not go straying into the later items. Is there a clear -- I asked you question a few minutes ago: Is there a clear distinguishing feature of item 14?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I wanted to tell you. I have an assumption as to who their leader was, and that was the distinction among the uniforms that follow on the list.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want us to proceed carefully, please, here, Witness. And I'm not blocking off that question of the leader. We'll come to that. But in the first place, can we just concentrate on the physical feature of item 14, without any question of where it leads. Can you say -- this is actually the third time I've asked you this question, so please answer it. Was there a clear, distinguishing physical feature which separates item 14 from the other items on your list?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll read it out to you. A uniform with workers' trousers, blue, combined with a military SMB shirt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the reference to SMB shirt, which is the first time you've given us that under this item, that's actually noted on your list there under item 14, is it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 14 is a uniform including workers' trousers, colour blue, combined with a military olive-grey shirt.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And you were saying, then, that from that physical observation, you -- well, you said you made an assumption. Are you saying in fact you had something to show you from which you could infer who the leader was, the leader of the people wearing item 14?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know, nor was I able to recognise, their leaders. I only have my assumptions. I know that five or ten of them were dressed in this uniform, and I assume that they were all under one leader.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Simply from the fact that they were dressed similarly?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what's your item 15?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A uniform including denim trousers, combined with a military SMB short, worn by Captain Dragan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Worn only by Captain Dragan?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He wore that uniform and a couple of men who accompanied him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What colour were the denim trousers?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The usual: Light blue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And in what way did those trousers then differ from item 14?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were different in terms of quality and colour. Those trousers were denim, so-called jeans, whereas the other trousers were the bottoms of workers' uniform, of lower quality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the colour was blue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what's item 16?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a uniform including SMB-colour trousers, combined with all sorts of civilian-type shirts of different colours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And item 17?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Uniforms worn by snipers, i.e., black leather suits from head to toe. Generally speaking, they wore weapons with sights, sniper rifles.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the black leather suit, head to toe, you're talking about something that goes right over the top of somebody's head, just leaving a part of the face exposed, are you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. They didn't wear anything on their heads.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, head to toe was your expression. So --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction. It was just an expression. Complete uniform.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I say from head to toe, I mean the body.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you, interpreter. That does certainly clarify things. I'll just -- Your Honour, I'll make that absolutely clear with the witness, then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The phrase that came across to me implied something else, Witness. You're saying this was -- was it a one-piece leather body suit that went up to the neck?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. Those were not one-piece suits. They had tops and bottoms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I had put to you what I thought might get us quickly to the answer. I had better ask you to describe specifically this particular item of clothing, item 17. Please do.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Black leather trousers. Black vest, black shirt, black gloves without fingertips. They had nothing on their heads. Everything made of leather.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The vest and the shirt made of leather?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just to clarify: A leather -- some sort of leather undershirt, then, and a leather shirt on top of that? Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Item 18?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Civilian clothing of different colours, combined with black hats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Item 19?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I noticed that those people wearing such hats went from house to house, broke in, and took away people's cars.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And took away other items as well?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I noticed at that time, and later on they were involved in all sorts of things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but to be clear: At this point, you're saying that they were taking away people's cars and then they were breaking into house and taking belongings out of the houses as well, were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whatever took their fancy. If they found weaponry, they would take that. But most of all they were interested in cars and they were looking for leather things, pieces of leather clothing. That's what interested them most.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Item 19?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Black uniforms with black leather hats, with a sign of skull and crossbones. I noticed on all people wearing that that they were the only ones wearing insignia denoting their affiliation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what did that particular skull and crossbones marking indicate to you, if anything?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: We all know well that that is the emblem and the symbol of Chetniks.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then item 20?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Civilian clothing, combined with woolen hats, with slits cut for eyes and mouths.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So that's a balaclava helmet, as it's called?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What colour?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly black.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Item 21?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Men who wore tracksuits and sports clothing, as if they hadn't had time to get hold of any real equipment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I'm not asking you to speculate as to why they were wearing this stuff, but what sort of sports clothing? You're talking about a tracksuit, are you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The kind worn by people who go to fitness centres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So these people were wearing tracksuits of that type with high military boots, were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of them wore high-leg military boots.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Over their tracksuits or under their tracksuits?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the bottom part of the trouser leg was pushed inside the boot. That's the way the JNA army wore them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned the JNA army. JNA army members didn't wear sports tracksuits in this way, did they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but they wore boots.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Item 22?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Volunteers who, for the most part, wore civilian clothing. I had occasion to be in direct contact with them, and they said that they had volunteered to do guard duty in certain parts of town and on certain streets.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So item 22, as a description of clothing, as a description of some sort of uniform, it's not actually that at all; it's just ordinary civilian clothing. Correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And item 23?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 23, persons who drove vehicles, procured the other ones that ammunition. They were dressed in a combination of clothing, such as SMB-colour trousers with different tops. Their job was to drive vehicles for supply and bring ammunition to those who were holding positions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it seems that what is distinguishing the people brought under item 23 is not in fact what they were physically wearing but the particular job that you saw them doing; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was the job they were doing, and what attracted my attention was the boots they wore and the clothing they wore, because the clothing was all colours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So can we be clear about a couple of things? Are you saying that every single -- we're talking about men in every case, aren't we? There are no women involved in any of the descriptions that you've given of any of these clothing items; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can answer that straight away.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This uniform under item 11 --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That uniform was sometimes worn by women, civilian defence or civilian protection, whatever you want to call it. But there were not many of them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did they wear high military boots?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the civilian defence and Territorial Defence did not wear boots. They wore high-leg shoes. That was the normal combination.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For men and women?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both men and women wore ankle-deep shoes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right. So far as all these other items are concerned, 1 to 23, are you saying that everybody, leaving aside what you've just said, but everybody in those categories was wearing high military boots?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apart from items 11 and 12, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your description that you gave a little bit earlier, you said that everybody had -- just remind us what dates you're talking about. You said: Everybody in the first place had a white ribbon around the arm. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: On that day, the 4th of May, 1992, that's what they wore. That was the emblem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On which arm?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The left arm, or the left shoulder.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel please get closer to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it was just a white ribbon, was it, going right round the upper arm or very close to the shoulder?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Either up here on the shoulder or tied around the arm with a tip hanging from the arm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you say that every single person in any of these 23 categories was wearing that white band?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On which day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The 4th of May, 1992. And I would see them also on the 5th of May. But on the 4th of May, everybody wore that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as far as you could see, what did that signify?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a distinguishing mark, a way of recognising each other as people involved in the operation to take over the town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the civilians that you described as breaking into people's houses and taking people's cars, all the people in that category had these white ribbons on the 4th of May as well, did they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't think you've ever mentioned anything about this white ribbon before, Witness, have you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wanted to explain this to you a moment ago and you didn't let me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I apologise if you are not being sufficient opportunity, Witness, but you have it now.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A moment ago I was about to shorten my description and not describe each uniform. In particular, I was going to divide them into two categories, the first half and the second half. And according to my logic and my understanding, those people were those who were engaged from the outside. Paramilitaries, i.e., locals organised in units of 10 or 15 were marked with these ribbons, organised unrests, and all sorts of trouble, and sometimes they didn't recognise each other and would shoot and hurt one another.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it is correct, isn't it, that until this morning, you have never, either in this case or in giving evidence before this Tribunal in a previous case, you have never mentioned this apparent distinguishing feature of a white ribbon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably nobody was interested before, and I didn't need to mention it. But I tried to mention all the uniforms I had seen and noticed. And the only distinguishing thing that was really remarkable on them all was the boots, because the boots were unavailable on the market. You couldn't buy them anywhere, and only the JNA had them, which means, in my opinion, all of that was organised, in cooperation with the JNA and in collusion with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I just take a moment to clarify something by way of instructions?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please do so and take care that your microphone is off.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Yes, of course. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then you described earlier this morning how a couple of days later there was a change to, I think you said a purple and white ribbon. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you remember exactly when that change took place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember exactly, but I think it was on the third day. So the 4th, 5th, the 6th -- either on the 6th or the 7th of May, the colour of the ribbons changed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was a sort of double ribbon, was it? Was it with a purple arm band and then a white band joined together?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please describe, then.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a ribbon with a pattern of purple and white. I can explain how this came about. They had to change --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Stop, please, unless this is going to answer the question. Start with a simple description, not in detail, but was it a zigzag pattern, a check pattern? Just of that order, some description.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. They were vertical. They actually made the ribbons from a piece of cloth and that's how it turned out. They were just short lines of white/purple, white purple, white purple not along the length of it but crosswise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many people, as far as you remember, in total did you personally see wearing this, as you've described it, purple and white ribbon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In order to avoid confusion like earlier, I just wanted to tell you briefly why this was done. Different groups of people tried to infiltrate themselves wearing these white ribbons, which did not have --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you. The question was how many people you saw wearing them. Would you please first answer the question, and if there's any need to explain, then do that after you've answered the question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very well. Thank you. According to my estimate and from what I saw when I was passing, it was about 1.000 people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was that a similar number to those that you had seen Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. previously wearing the white ribbon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was there any overlap in time when some people were still wearing the white ribbon and some were wearing the purple and white ribbon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They had to change it at the same time for all of those who were there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not asking what they had to do; I'm asking whether, from your observation, was there any time when you saw an overlap with some people still wearing the white ribbon and others wearing the purple and white ribbon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And can you say how long was that period of overlap?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps a day or two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I'd asked you a few moments ago about the fact that you had never previously mentioned these ribbons, and I think you said that, well, nobody had asked you or nobody seemed to be interested. Witness, it must have been, I suggest, very clear to you when you were first approached and interviewed in relation to these matters that the question of coordination and organisation and planning of military or paramilitary forces in Brcko in early May 1992 was absolutely central to what you were being asked about, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I explained to them everything that they wanted to know. They didn't ask me that question, so I didn't tell them anything about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, would you say it's fair to say about yourself that you're not always a man who has to wait to be asked before you give any information? Is that a fair description?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you ask me something, I will give you an answer. I am now trying for the second time to explain something to you, and you are not allowing me to do that. So what I'm trying to explain to you and to tell you, to make it easier for you to continue with your work, will not be recorded in the transcript or in the investigation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Witness. You just had to give me a moment to fathom what it was you were saying then.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: With my first example, I tried to tell you about this uniform of the civilian and the Territorial Defence, and about these people in the black leather uniforms. Now I'm trying to explain to you about the ribbons and you are stopping me. I wanted to tell you one thing: When they decided to change the colour of the ribbon, they -- some people came in an organised fashion in order to rob and loot, and they were not aware that they had to change the colour of the ribbon, and that is how you could tell them apart. Then the others, the officers, took steps to see who these people were, what they were. So there were people who were arriving in an unorganised manner. They didn't belong to any units, were not subordinated to anyone. They came independently in order to loot in that area. Now you have the explanation why the colour of the ribbon was changed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you saying that you were observing or personally aware of all this at the time, of instructions being given by officers for changes of ribbons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not through the officers, but I had some friends, I had company with whom I was in touch. I was on good terms with them, so they would come by to see how we were doing, and then sometimes they would tell us something, they would give us some information. And on one of those occasions, it was about the colour of the ribbons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You see, Witness, the most obvious reason why you might not have mentioned such a clear and quite graphic point as the change of the ribbons is that you're now grossly exaggerating the position as it actually was in May 1992. Isn't that what you're doing?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am just trying to explain and to make the work of this Tribunal easier, so that it would be informed about this date and a couple of days later and all that I had gone through. The reason why I didn't provide that information before, I cannot be responsible for that, because the people who came to take my statement didn't ask me about that. They were interested in something else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the -- in your witness statement, you say that by the 4th of May, the Serb offensive was complete and the Serb forces occupied Brcko up to the river -- is it Brka? I -- you know which river I'm talking about? I hope my pronunciation is near enough.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: By "the Serb forces," you're talking about all these forces that you've, in effect, listed in items 1 to 23, are you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the river -- this river is not the main river, of course, is it? This is the river that joins the main river?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the river we're talking about, the smaller river, the tributary, effectively cuts the town of Brcko more or less in half, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it runs broadly north/south. It winds, but it's much more north/south than east/west, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Its source is in the south, and in the north it flows into the River Sava.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Well, strictly south/north, then, if we're talking about the river's flow. And the occupation of -- by Serb forces, then, up to the river was from which direction?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the direction of Bijeljina -- generally from the direction of Bijeljina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is that from the west or from the east?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the east.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And then what was stopping them, then, from occupying over the river on the 4th of May?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't tell you exactly, but on the 4th of May, when all of them came up to the River Brka, there was an organised attempt to move out the population from that part of town, which was mostly inhabited by Muslims - I say Muslims mostly, but there were some Serbs and Croats amongst them too - in order to save those people. Some groups self-organised themselves and tried to put up resistance, but that's when shooting broke out from infantry weapons, from rifles, and this stopped for a couple of days, until all of these people moved out, those of them who wanted to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart, it's close to 10.30. Would this be a suitable moment?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: It will be as suitable as any moment coming up in the next few minutes, Your Honour, certainly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Usher, could you first escort the witness out of the courtroom. Mr. 018, we'll have a break for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stewart, how much time do you think you'll still need to finish cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Probably something getting on for one hour, Your Honour. I doubt more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You are aware that, of course, as the first 92 bis witness, that the time allocated for cross-examining 92 bis witnesses is 50 hours. I wonder for how many in the future you'd ask for cross-examination, and perhaps it would be a good idea that you give a time indication for the 92 bis witnesses you'd like to cross-examine.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Does Your Honour mean specifically in advance of each witness or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, we all might have had the experience in life that time seems to be sufficient at the beginning of an exercise and when we proceed, that sometimes we become aware that time becomes more and more precious and that we, as a matter of fact, would need more time to accomplish what we had in mind. At this pace, taking another hour, that would bring us approximately to, I would say, a little bit over three hours, within 50 hours you could cross-examine not more than 15 witnesses. Of course, if the Defence decides it allows for cross-examination only for 15 witnesses, of course, but it's a long list of 92 bis witnesses and it is of some concern.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I comment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Leaving aside, I suppose, the fact that today we're indirectly then helping the Court not to waste time. But the -- but may we suggest, respectfully, that at this very early stage in the case, there's no special value in attempting to extrapolate from the early cross-examinations to global figures, because if -- I could say this: If every time a Rule 92 bis witness comes to be cross-examined, it's necessary for him to produce a list of 22 items and go through them, then the estimate would have to be radically revised. So, Your Honour, may we simply ask for a little bit of preliminary indulgence at this point so we see where we're going?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you are telling this Chamber that your time management will be such that you'll not have any problems at a later stage, then of course we will entirely leave it in your hands. And it's good to know for the Chamber that not every witness will have to produce a list of 22 or 23 uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Well, I hope not, Your Honour. You never know what witness are going to produce. But, Your Honour, I didn't in fact wish to make such a sweepingly bold statement as to say we're not going to run into problems in the future. What we are going to do, as we promised Your Honour, we're going to attempt to cross-examine each witness as much as necessary and no more. I hope that's what I'm doing with this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. As you know, necessity is a flexible concept. We'll adjourn for 20 minutes. We'll restart at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber only received two minutes ago the submission of the Defence this morning, so let's first take a next break to read it. Has the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: We have just received it as well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. So then we'll see how much time we'll need. The witness may be escorted into the courtroom again. Are the technicians instructed not to show his face? And is the public gallery empty? It is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please be seated, Witness 018. Mr. Stewart, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I asked you before the break about the occupation, as you've described it, of the Serb forces up to the River Brka, and I had asked you, but I'm going to ask you again, what it was and who it was, if anybody, who prevented the Serb forces from occupying over the river, on the 4th and 5th of May.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that, but it seems that maybe you didn't hear it. Certain groups organised themselves, five or six such groups, which had hunting weapons. They were trying to stop the breakthrough or the incursions of these units who had taken the town and they prevented them from taking over the whole of the town. They were successful in doing this for a day or two, during which time the population which was on that side of the river, and also those who wanted to leave their homes, were able to leave in the direction of Majevica.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean five or six groups, or groups of five or six men?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Groups of five or six men.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when you referred a moment ago to certain groups organised themselves, five or six such groups, that was just a slip of the tongue, was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Five to six people in these groups. There were two or three such groups, which on the 4th of May and the 5th of May prevented them from crossing the River Brka.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So about 15 to 20 men on the other side of the river prevented the Serb forces, as you've labelled them, from crossing the river; is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the -- remind us what you say was the total number of the Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to my estimate, there were about 1.000 of them, up to the River Brka. So they were on the side which they had already occupied. This is what I saw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were you -- the way you're describing it, you seem to have been -- this is intended neutrally. You seem to have been dedicated that day to observing yourself what was going on. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of this happened from the point when we were arrested, taken to an assembly point, and then, from that location, taken to the police station, and then another 50 metres further, to the old hotel. That's the stretch in which I saw all of that. I could see what all of these different armies were doing. So these were my observations over a stretch of 500 metres.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, a lot of what you are now telling the Tribunal about the events in Brcko is information, so far as it's true, which you have obtained since then and got from other people, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This information about crossing over and taking the other side of town, we received from a person who came back from the other side of the line. He was a Serb, and he happened to be in this unit which tried to break through and take that other part of town. And since they did not manage to do that, he came back and he was very angry, and then he did what he did after that. So we can also speak about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What we will do, Witness, is we'll speak about things in the sense of I'll ask questions and then please continue to answer them. The description -- let's start with this assumption. I don't suppose either you, and certainly not I, are military strategists, Witness, but let's start with, I think, a common-sense piece of knowledge that it takes fewer men to defend than to attack. That's simply conventional, common knowledge. But from what you know about Brcko, the idea that 15 to 20 men could prevent hundreds and hundreds, up to a thousand, men from crossing the river is just ridiculous, isn't it, from what you know of your own town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to give you an explanation to that question as well. Those people whom I mentioned, about 1.000 of them, did not all take part in the offensive and try to cross over. What they were doing is trying, in groups of 10, 15, 20, or up to 50 people, they were trying to take the road, which was a key road. It's the road that passes through Brcko and goes to Bijeljina, Banja Luka, Belgrade, Knin. This was important for them. They were trying to take that road, and they didn't manage to do that until they got reinforcements, and then, after a day or two, managed to take that road. I think that I was clear. I'm trying to help you so that you would understand the general objectives and the layout of the town as it looked. The SUP building, where we were all assembled, is not more than 50 metres away from the Brka River, so you could see everything from there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But your description there, Witness, of what they were trying to do and trying to take the road, and so on, that can't possibly be from your own firsthand observation at that time, can it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you right away the name of the person who tried to do that. It was Goran Jelisic, with his group. He tried to take the road, and did not succeed. When he came back from there, then he committed what he did, together with this group, and I was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you seem, then, to be confirming the suggestion that I put to you, which is that that particular description by you of what the Serb forces were trying to do and what they were failing to do is not your own knowledge and observation at all, but which is information which you say you got from somebody else.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Directly from Goran Jelisic. That's where the information came from.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your statement, you refer to an incident where Serbian soldiers were killed. If you'd like to refresh your memory, this is paragraph 19 of your statement. Have you still got your statement with you, or can it be given to you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I think this is pretty familiar to you by now, but this is -- you're describing an incident involving Mr. Jelisic, but then, in particular, I'm asking you about the last two or three lines there. It's the last two sentences, in English: "The man asked him why he was beating him, and Jelisic said they, meaning the Serbs, were trying to do good by him while the non-Serbs were killing him. By this he was referring to an incident where Serbian soldiers were killed." And then you give the beaten man's name. What incident was that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's exactly what I was talking about a little earlier, when Goran Jelisic, with his group of men, tried to occupy this road. They were met by the citizens who live in that part of town. Shooting broke out. What he told us, that there were dead, this was just some kind of excuse for what he did. Because later, through questions and information that we received, we found out that there were wounded, but there were no killed. He was angry because this operation was not successful, and then he did what he did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you go, please, to paragraph 30 of your statement.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you see that says: "I knew Bolero and he asked us what we were doing. We told him Jelisic had told us to wait in the park." And then it's the last sentence I just want to ask you about: "Bolero told us." And the way it reads, this is the English version, but the way it reads is: "Bolero told us he did like what was happening and he told us to accompany him." Now, I'm not sure: First of all, does the version that you have got in your own language, does it say "Bolero told us he did like what was happening," or does it say that "Bolero told us he did not like what was happening"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was looking over my statement, I noticed this mistake and I reacted right away, and I asked that this be corrected to: "Bolero told us that he did not like what was happening." And he told us to accompany him." Again, I would like to stress that he did not like what was happening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, Witness, I'm not going to challenge you on that. That seems to be the obvious sense of your statement. So that correction can be treated as made now to your statement and your evidence, can't it? You nod, but the transcript doesn't pick up nodding.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: Would Your Honour give me a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: No further cross-examination, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stewart. Has the cross-examination raised any issue on which the Prosecution would like to re-examine the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes. If I may, Your Honour, I have three areas, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you. Re-examined by Mr. Hannis:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness 018, you were asked about the 23 different groups. I wanted to ask you a couple of questions about that clothing. Apart from groups number 18, 19, and 20, where you told us about black hats, skull-and-crossbones hats, and ski mask, did any of these other groups wear any particular kind of headgear that distinguished them?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you tell us, please, which groups and what kind of headgear.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I indicated those old military uniforms, and the men who wore them, for the most part, wore old Serbian peasant hats. There were also some other people who wore the same fur-lined hats, but not with the skull-and-crossbones sign, but the elongated type. They were sort of pulled upwards, looked taller.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Any others?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw them on the 4th of May. After that day, I was not allowed to move around, so I couldn't see any more.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness 018, I wanted to ask you about the ribbons. You mentioned that you were told about this by some friends. Can you tell the Court, without naming names at this point, but can you tell us who these people were? Were they Serbs? Were they Muslims? Were they Croats?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Serbs who worked as reserve policemen in town.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And were there other people present with you when you were told this, and did those people hear the same thing you did?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: May I have one moment, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness 018. Those are all the questions I have, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Hannis. It seems to be that no new issues have been raised in this re-examination that should not be done, so I take it the Defence has no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STEWART
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge El Mahdi has one or more questions for you. Questioned by the Court: JUDGE EL MAHDI: Thank you, Mr. President. [Interpretation] Witness, I would like to clear up certain points. The first of them concerns what you call volunteers of Captain Dragan. First of all, how do you know that they were volunteers? And I will explain. In your statement, you said, and I'm quoting what you said in English: [In English] "Dragan was wearing a military shirt with no insignia. He wore jeans and military boots. The two soldiers with him wore the summer fatigues of the JNA." [Interpretation] So, judging by their appearance, they probably belonged to JNA groups, and you say that they were volunteers. So how do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can explain. Captain Dragan was together with a group of people who did not belong to his units. He carried out operations of arresting people in house-to-house rounds and brought them to the hotel, whereas people from his unit were securing the old SUP building and the building where we were detained. So they were not together. And I can tell you at the same time how I found out that those were men of Captain Dragan. They told us themselves that they were volunteers, namely, Captain Dragan's Volunteers, and they even told us from which towns they came from. Kosovska Mitrovica, Belgrade, Vukovar, Valjevo, Bor, Majdanpek. All those men were engaged in providing security to the SUP building and the old Posavina Hotel. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] But from what you know, was Captain Dragan himself part of JNA troops?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot make any claims about that. I cannot tell you exactly. He would just show up from time to time, and when he was there, he told us that his name was Captain Dragan. And he would ask us one question and was angry to hear the answer. And as to which unit he belonged to, some volunteer unit or a JNA unit, I really don't know. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] All right. I'll move on to another subject. You said that on the 4th of May, or probably before the 4th of May, you lived with your sister, and for all practical purposes, you lived in the basement. Is that correct? Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's true that I was in the basement on the 4th of May. That's where we took cover. Because a general all-out offensive started on the 4th and there was a lot of shooting from all sorts of weapons, including heavy weaponry, and all of us tried to find safety in the basement, where we were found by Captain Dragan and his men, who took us away. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Yes, but you say that the troops, and I quote, "Serb troops," Serb forces, I'm quoting again: "The Serbian forces -- [In English] to remove people from their houses." [Interpretation] What do you imply when you say "Serbian forces"?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in my mind, they started everything that happened in town, and they started the war. Because the general population, Muslim and Croat, who wanted to leave, left. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Sorry to interrupt you, but I would like to know exactly how, in fact, in your opinion, when you say "the Serbian forces," who are you talking about? Are you talking about local Serbs, or who?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were very few locals who took part in that attack. Other people, other groups, came from outside, and the most distinguishing feature were those traditional three-finger signs on a raised hand and the singing of Chetnik songs. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Why am I asking this question? I want some clarity. Because you say in another paragraph that the soldiers who came for you and who were under the command of Captain Dragan were dressed in JNA uniforms.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] So you can confirm that the people who came to search your house and who tried to arrest you were dressed in JNA uniforms, at least as far as uniform is concerned.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] And I'm now moving to another subject. After your arrest, and after your release, you returned to the house of your sister?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to the same place where they took me away from. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] So the house itself was not taken over by anybody else?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] And later, I believe you went to your apartment, which was still vacant; it hadn't been taken over by anyone.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Two and a half months later, that is, two and a half months after the 4th of May, I returned to my apartment. There was no one there. But there were soldiers, both outside and inside the building, although my apartment was empty. JUDGE EL MAHDI: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have got a few questions for you as well. May I first ask a question directly related to your last answer. You answered to the question of Judge El Mahdi that you, two and a half months after the 4th of May, you returned to your apartment. That would then be mid-July. In your statement --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- you say that you were arrested on the 13th of July. Could you explain how it happened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: One day, an acquaintance of mine came - he worked in the reserve police force - intending to tell me to go back to my apartment because a list of apartments and apartment owners was being made. I asked him that he let me go with him, because he lived in the same building. And he told me: "You are a local man. You were born in this town. You are free to leave. Nobody would harm you." The very next day, I went to the building and spent about two hours waiting outside before I was allowed to go into my apartment. The day after, an inspection team came, inspected my apartment, checked my ID, and issued me with some instructions as to how I was to conduct myself in my own apartment. Several days later, a raid was carried out around town. People were rounded up and taken to the Batkovici camp. I was in that group.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That answers my question, so could you confirm that you did not stay for the full two and a half months in your sister's house, but a little bit over two months?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't spend even ten days in my apartment. The rest of the time I lived at my sister's place. After I came to my apartment, I was listed as the owner of the apartment, residing there alone, and the person who came to warn me and to give me those instructions, all this happened within the ten days before we were taken away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just stop you there. I see that your testimony that you stayed for two and a half months was not very precise in this respect, because it should have been a bit shorter. My next question is whether any reasons were given to you why you were taken to the Batkovici camp.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A general explanation given to all of us who were rounded up on that occasion was that we were being taken away to do labour, that there were jobs to be done and that we were being taken away to do them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Were you ever interviewed when you were in the Batkovic camp?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was never interrogated at the camp. Only on one occasion when I asked to be seen by a doctor, the lieutenant colonel of the Bijeljina garrison came. I was questioned as to my medical history before I was released to go home again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: In your statement, you say that you returned to Brcko because you were sick. Could you tell us what ailments you were suffering from.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS KRAJ-018 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had inflammation of joints twice in my life, and I was paralysed during those two times, and everybody who knows anything about it knows that inflammation of the joints is accompanied by heart problems.
